description.narrative: Morocco - Artisan And Fez Medina Project - Fez Medina Activity: This activity includes the rehabilitation or construction of five sites along the Fez Medina tourist routes. Specifically, MCC Funding will support the following: (i) the design of the Makina, reconstruction of portions of the Makina, and the design and reconstruction of Place Lalla Ydouna ("PLY") and three 14th and 15 century fondouks (large, multi-story structures surrounding a central courtyard); (ii) a design competition to create effectively designed spaces at the Makina and PLY that will better serve local residents and attract visitors to Fez; (iii) the development of a production zone at Ain Nokbi for the resettlement of copperware workers affected by the rehabilitation of PLY; and (iv) a study to identify and evaluate options for the traditional tanneries that are consistent with reducing poverty and stimulating economic growth and that meet relevant national and international environmental, health and safety standards.
City of Fez, Morocco

condition.narrative: 40) Before entering into any contract(s) with consultants to conduct any EIA or perform any design work for the Fez Medina Project Activity, MCA-Morocco shall establish an environmental and social unit within ADER-Fez (to be in a form and with a scope of responsibility satisfactory to MCC). Such environmental and social unit shall remain in place and shall be sufficiently staffed and mobilized (to MCC's satisfaction) throughout the term of the Compact

41) MCA-Morocco shall establish an advisory committee to coordinate the activities of the other agencies and stakeholders in connection with the Fez Medina Project Activity, and such committee shall remain in place and shall be sufficiently staffed and mobilized (to MCC's satisfaction) throughout the term of the Compact

42) MCA-Morocco shall ensure that, satisfactory to MCC, 1) an EIA and site-specific EMPs are completed for Ain Nokbi, the fondouks; 2) an Environmental, Health and Safety Audit (EHSA) has been conducted for PLY and the Makina; 3) a RAP has been developed and implemented in accordance with the World Bank Policy on Involuntary Resettlement (OP4.12); and, 4) an EIA and site-specific EMPs are developed for PLY and the Makina following the design competition

43) The development, implementation and enforcement of a sanitary and waste management plan for Place Lalla Ydouna, including the completion of the RADEEF plan to eliminate the transmission of wastewater via the river
44) The Government has caused to be mobilized $40 million in funding to finance the completion of the Makina sub-activity.
Further details on conditions precedent affecting this activity can be found in the top-level parent activities.
